request.description: A single square dungeon floor tile of old grey stone, seen from above, filling the whole frame edge to edge. Flagstones set into bare rock, worn smooth and slightly dished down the middle where centuries of foot traffic have polished them, grime walked into the joints until it is part of the surface. A quiet surface: one large flat field of stone with only two or three small texture events near the edges, the centre left open. Nothing is broken and nothing has collapsed; the stone is used up, not ruined. Nothing decorative, nothing arranged, no objects placed on it. Lit by one strong key light from the upper left: painted white highlights along every upward-facing and left-facing edge, and the surfaces facing down and to the right dropped into painted shade, so the direction the light comes from is unmistakable in the artwork itself.

Rough grey found stone with heavy orc-made timber pinned into it — squared beams lashed twice with rope, driven iron pins, a hide strap, a salvaged plank laid flat over an older repair. Over-built and correct: every band, strap and pin is holding something and nothing is there to be looked at. Stone and timber both rubbed smooth where shoulders and hands pass. Nothing is broken and nothing has collapsed; it is used up, not ruined. Lit by one strong key light from the upper left: painted white highlights along every upward-facing and left-facing edge, and the surfaces facing down and to the right dropped into painted shade, so the direction the light comes from is unmistakable in the artwork itself.

request.description: A single square dungeon floor tile of old grey stone, seen from above, filling the whole frame edge to edge. Flagstones set into bare rock, worn smooth and slightly dished down the middle where centuries of foot traffic have polished them, grime walked into the joints until it is part of the surface. A quiet surface: one large flat field of stone with only two or three small texture events near the edges, the centre left open. Nothing is broken and nothing has collapsed; the stone is used up, not ruined. Nothing decorative, nothing arranged, no objects placed on it. Evenly illuminated from the front with no key light and no cast shadows, so no direction of light is declared anywhere in the artwork. Form is carried by the material itself: joints, recesses and undercuts sit darker because they are enclosed, raised and exposed surfaces sit lighter, and different materials hold plainly different values. No white highlights, no glints, no specular edges, no light source.

Rough grey found stone with heavy orc-made timber pinned into it — squared beams lashed twice with rope, driven iron pins, a hide strap, a salvaged plank laid flat over an older repair. Over-built and correct: every band, strap and pin is holding something and nothing is there to be looked at. Stone and timber both rubbed smooth where shoulders and hands pass. Nothing is broken and nothing has collapsed; it is used up, not ruined. Completely flat and unlit. Every material is one single solid value with no shading of any kind — no highlights, no shadows, no gradients, no darkening inside joints or recesses, no soft edges. Surfaces are told apart only by the flat colour value of the material each one is made of.
